text: Philip Rubin received his BA in psychology and linguistics from Brandeis University and his PhD in experimental psychology from the University of Connecticut. His research combines computational, engineering, linguistic, physiological, and psychological approaches to study embodied cognition, especially the biological bases of speech and language. He is best known for his work on articulatory synthesis, speech perception, sinewave synthesis, and theoretical models of speech production and perception. Rubin developed key software systems such as ASY and SWS at Haskins Laboratories, and co-founded AVISA and the Talking Heads website. He served in leadership roles at the National Science Foundation and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, focusing on cognitive science, neuroscience, and behavioral research. He is also active in science policy, ethics, and advocacy, including work on human subjects research and emerging technologies. Rubin has received numerous honors, including fellowships from the Acoustical Society of America, the American Psychological Association, and the IEEE, and is a member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. He is currently the President of the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences and the Chair of the Board of Directors of Haskins Laboratories.
